title: CAN bus
summary: Bus breaks, duplicate ids, CANivore, termination, loose connectors.

start.question: What is the symptom?
start.help: Check in Phoenix Tuner X, the REV Hardware Client, or the DS Robot Power tab.

options.label: Two devices move together or one flickers
Devices on a CANivore are missing
Works on the cart, drops when the robot moves
DS shows CAN errors or bus utilization near 100 percent
Everything after one point in the chain

all-missing.title: Whole CAN bus is down
steps: Tug test the yellow and green CAN wires at the roboRIO CAN port. Yellow is CAN High, green is CAN Low.
Power off. Measure resistance across CAN High and CAN Low at the RIO. About 60 ohms is good. 120 ohms means a terminator is missing. Open means a break at the RIO.
Check the PDH or PDP is powered and its CAN termination jumper is ON if it sits at the end of the chain.
Look at the first device after the RIO. Talon FX alternating red or Spark MAX flashing means the break is between it and the RIO.

steps.text: Are devices still missing from the bus?
steps.yes: Swap the RIO CAN connector wires.

chain-break.title: Chain is broken at one point
steps: Find the last device that still shows up and the first that does not. The break is between them.
Tug test every crimp and connector between those two. Pull each wire, not the housing.
Confirm yellow goes to yellow and green to green at every joint. One swapped pair kills everything after it.
Re-crimp the bad joint with ferrules or a proper crimper, not twisted wire.
Measure about 60 ohms across the bus. Open at the far end means the last terminator is missing. Replace it.

steps.yes: Replace the run between the two devices.

one-missing.title: One device is missing
steps: Check the device has power. No lights means its breaker, fuse, or power wires.
Tug test its CAN pigtail on both sides. A device mid-chain with one bad pigtail can still pass the bus through.
Check its ID in Tuner X or the Hardware Client. A new device ships as ID 0 or 1 and may not match the code.
Check the firmware year on the device. Old firmware is ignored by the new library. Update it.

steps.text: Is the device still missing from the bus?
steps.yes: Swap the device and set its ID with the team.

duplicate-ids.title: Duplicate CAN IDs
steps: Open Phoenix Tuner X. A red device card means two devices of the same model share an ID. The Hardware Client warns too.
Isolate one device at a time. Pull the breakers for the others, or unplug the bus after it.
Set a unique ID on each device. Write it on tape.
Redeploy code after changing IDs. Use your laptop with Tuner X if the team has none.

steps.text: Do devices still share an ID in Tuner X?
steps.yes: Isolate and re-ID the last device.

canivore-light.question: What is the CANivore STAT light doing?

canivore-usb.title: CANivore not talking to the roboRIO
steps: Wait for the RIO to finish booting. The CANivore enumerates over USB after boot.
Reseat the USB cable at both ends. Try the other RIO USB port.
Replace the USB cable. Long or unshielded cables fail. Keep it short, away from motor leads.
Check the CANivore has power on its own lead.
Static from an unshielded USB extension can kill both RIO USB ports. Check both ports on the RIO.

steps.text: Is the CANivore still dark or red on USB?

canivore-no-code.title: CANivore sees USB, no robot program
steps: Orange means USB is up but the robot code is not running or not using this bus.
Start the robot code. Confirm the DS shows Robot Code green.
Check the code uses the CANivore name in every device constructor on that bus. A blank bus name goes to the RIO bus.
Confirm Tuner X sees the CANivore with the same name the code uses.

steps.text: Are the CANivore devices still missing?
steps.yes: Review the constructor bus names with the team.

canivore-bus.title: CANivore is up, its bus is not
steps: The CANivore has one built-in terminator. The far end needs a 120 ohm resistor. Measure about 60 ohms across CANH and CANL with power off.
Tug test the CAN wires at the CANivore and along the chain.
Confirm the devices are on the CANivore chain, not the RIO chain. Mixed chains miss devices.
A Talon FX showing alternating red is not seeing the bus. Trace the wiring to it.

steps.text: Are devices still missing on the CANivore?
steps.yes: Fix the terminator or the bad joint.

intermittent.title: CAN drops when the robot moves
steps: Tug test every CAN connector with the robot on the cart. Pull each wire, not the plug body. The one that moves is the fault.
Look for CAN wires across a moving joint, near a chain, or pinched under a bumper mount.
Push every connector fully in. Latching connectors should click.
Tie-wrap the pigtail near each device so the crimp does not carry the load.
Measure about 60 ohms across the bus. Wiggle each joint and watch for an open.

steps.text: Does the bus still drop under movement?
steps.yes: Re-crimp the joint that reads open.

utilization.title: CAN errors or high bus utilization
steps: Open the DS Diagnostics tab. Utilization above about 80 percent drops frames. Errors climbing during a match mean a wiring fault or an overloaded bus.
Errors that climb only when the robot moves are a loose connector. Use the intermittent branch of this guide.
Move the drivetrain to a CANivore, or lower status frame rates on devices the code does not read.
Check for a device on old firmware sending frames the library does not expect. Update it.

steps.text: Are CAN errors or utilization still high?
steps.yes: Set status frame periods with the team.
